title: Cycle precommit calibration and emergency swap ledger
creator: Ayesha Malik
description: Create a lightweight precommit calibration runbook and a realtime 'Emergency Swap Ledger' to reduce mid-cycle firefighting. The deliverable will be a one-page precommit checklist, a small spreadsheet (ledger) for authorized emergency swaps, and a short engineering/PM playbook for executing swaps and verifying signal integrity after role changes. Goal: reduce mid-cycle scope loss and context-switch churn by providing clear rules and an auditable ledger for temporary staffing swaps.
acceptance_criteria: One-page precommit checklist published in Confluence and linked from Cycle kickoff doc
Emergency Swap Ledger template available in Google Drive with change history and guardrails
Swap execution playbook (2 pages) with clear owner handoff steps, verification steps, and rollback criteria
Run one live simulation during Cycle kickoff and capture 3 improvement actions
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng leads (infra, runtime), Design lead, and PM director
tasks: Create Emergency Swap Ledger template and permission model (owner: PM + Ops)
Work with Eng leads to define allowable swap windows and skill equivalency matrix
Draft execution playbook and quick-check verification steps
Run tabletop simulation with 3 teams and record timings/edge cases
Incorporate feedback and publish final artifacts
Add links to Console runbooks and Cycle kickoff agenda
risks: Ledger misuse if permissions not tightly controlled (mitigation: restrict edit rights to authorized roles)
Swaps causing regressions when critical context is lost (mitigation: mandatory 15m handoff and smoke tests)
Overly bureaucratic process that disincentivizes helpful swaps (mitigation: keep templates minimal and track time-to-swap metrics)
Dependency on Eng leads' bandwidth to evaluate skill equivalency (mitigation: provide suggested mappings and allow quick approval flow)
Simulated run may not surface production edge cases (mitigation: capture open issues and schedule follow-up postmortem)
